title: client.config.json
description: The single seam for all client-specific portal values (see docs/primitives/client-config.md). Loaded + validated against this schema by scripts/config.py on import and by the portal-verify gate. Key surface owned by #17; this schema mirrors it key-for-key.

$access_comment.$comment: Documentation-only sibling of the optional `access` block (#53); the engine never reads it.

client.$comment: Purpose-neutral owner seam (#206, Phase 2: canonical). `brain.*` is the documented, canonical form; `name`/`shortName`/`engagement` below are DEPRECATED read aliases for `brain.name`/`brain.shortName`/`brain.owner.name`/`brain.purpose`, accepted through one more release (2026-09-24 decision) and flagged by `make template-update`'s preview for an instance that still sets them, then removed. `scripts/init.py` no longer stamps them into a new scaffold. `slug`/`domain` are deploy identity, not part of the seam, and are not deprecated. `client` itself is optional, so a brain declared entirely under `brain.*` needs no `client` block at all. `client.config.json` stays the file name.

heroMark.description: Optional hero-mark image path (swapped for the inline generic mark at runtime on the home page)

heroMarkDark.description: Optional mark variant for dark chrome (e.g. a white wordmark); shown via the theme-aware logo-on-dark class while heroMark covers light chrome. Falls back to heroMark when absent.

heroMarkWidth.description: Optional hero-mark width (px int or CSS length)

owner.description: Owner / co-brand seam (#47): the party running the engagement, co-branded with the client across the portal chrome — topbar wordmark, home hero eyebrow, the co-brand stat, and every page footer. Accepts either the legacy string form (the owner name) or an object carrying name + artwork. Default name 'ACME'; set '' (or {"name": ""}) to drop the owner brand entirely. With no mark configured the chrome renders the owner NAME as a text wordmark, so an unbranded install carries no company's artwork.

name.description: Owner name used in the footer, hero eyebrow, co-brand stat, and as the text wordmark when no mark is set.

mark.description: Optional owner wordmark/logo image path used in the topbar and footer mark slots. Empty -> the name renders as a text wordmark.

markDark.description: Optional owner mark variant for dark chrome; shown via the theme-aware logo-on-dark class while `mark` covers light chrome. Falls back to `mark` when absent.

maxToolOutputChars.$comment: Caps the TOTAL tool-result text fed back per chat request (one document is capped by maxDocChars). Over budget, results truncate with a visible marker; the request never fails. Default 600000 when absent.

docRoots.$comment: Top-level directories read_doc may read. Absent/empty = the whole served corpus.

requires.description: Page-set: the profile overlay this page belongs to. The page is registered only when profile.overlays selects it (or it is the base); a config with no overlays registers every page.

substrate.description: Vector substrate, graduating independently of brain.store.

storage_mode.description: The files-cell writer: json-commit edits a source JSON record and commits it through the GitHub Contents API. A brain with a declared brain.authority is written only by that authority's governed writer and delivered through its projections (docs/design/adr-authority-per-brain-kind.md); the Worker never writes it.

name.$comment: Purpose-neutral owner seam (#206, Phase 2: canonical). The brain's own display name — the documented, canonical field; `scripts/init.py` stamps it directly for a new scaffold. Falls back to the deprecated `client.name` alias via scripts/config.py / config.js when absent (accepted for one more release).

shortName.$comment: Compact form for tight UI (headers/footers), read by app/nav.js's brainShortName(). Canonical (#206, Phase 2); falls back to the deprecated `client.shortName` alias, then to `brain`/`client` `name`, when absent.

purpose.$comment: What this brain is for, e.g. what `init --purpose` will stamp (#200). Canonical (#206, Phase 2); falls back to the deprecated `client.engagement` alias when absent.

owner.$comment: Who the brain belongs to: a person (an individual's brain) or an organization (a company/client brain) — distinct from `branding.owner`, the co-brand identity of whoever RUNS the portal (#47). Canonical (#206, Phase 2); falls back to {kind: organization, name: client.name} — the deprecated alias — when absent.

blobs.description: Where non-markdown artifacts live. Graduates independently of `store`; reported in the manifest's substrate block.

stores.description: Where this environment finds each store the adopted contract.json declares (docs/design/substrate-matrix.md). contract.json owns the topology; `id` matches a contract `stores[].id` and `dsn` is a reference, never a literal location.

store.description: The adopted contract's authority store id; its connection comes from the matching `brain.stores[].dsn`. A sqlite or files store resolves to a path under _internal/.

projections.description: CI freshness mode for delivered projections (docs/design/adr-authority-per-brain-kind.md). committed: receipted app/projections/<consumer>.json are committed and verified by check-projection-receipts. live: nothing delivered is committed; the authority is read at request time.

sourceAdapters.description: Explicit generic projections; matching documents/tracker/activity ontology overlays required. Activity reads only an explicitly frozen snapshot. Defaults to none. Does not grant read access.

goldenRecords.description: Golden-record verifiability gate (#65): a curated set of must-be-true assertions about the corpus, checked on every build (scripts/check-golden-records.py). Empty/absent -> clean no-op, same convention as access/staleness. Each entry names a JSON artifact, a dot-path field within it, and the exact value that field must equal.

description.description: Human-readable name for this assertion, shown in a failure.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the JSON artifact, e.g. 'app/decisions.json'.

field.description: Dot-path into the parsed JSON, e.g. 'decisions.0.status' or 'count'. Array indices are plain integers in the path.

equals.description: The exact value the field must equal (deep-equal; any JSON type).

terminologyCanon.description: Terminology canon gate (#65): a config-driven deprecated-term lint over the same knowledge.sources roots gen-knowledge-pack.py/gen-docs-manifest.py already walk (scripts/check-terminology-canon.py). Empty/absent -> clean no-op, same convention as access/staleness/goldenRecords.

deprecated.description: term/phrase -> why it's banned (what replaces it, shown in a failure). Case-insensitive, word-boundary matched.

contentConsistency.description: Cross-file content-consistency gate (#65): the same fact stated in more than one artifact must agree (scripts/check-content-consistency.py). Unlike goldenRecords (a field must equal a FIXED declared value), this checks two declared fact sites against each other. Empty/absent -> clean no-op, same convention as access/staleness/goldenRecords/terminologyCanon.

description.description: Human-readable name for this pair, shown in a failure.

path.description: Repo-relative path to the first JSON artifact.

field.description: Dot-path into the first artifact's parsed content. Array indices are plain integers in the path.

matches.description: The second fact site, same shape as path/field above.

access.$comment: Identity-aware read scoping (#53), enforced by access.js + worker.js on an Access-authenticated host. OPTIONAL and OFF by default: with no `access` key the engine serves exactly what it always did. Model: a DENYLIST of path globs (`restricted`) that only `owners` may read, plus per-entry `owners` when one restricted set has its own readers. An owner spec is either a full email (exact match) or a bare local-part, which matches that local-part at ANY domain — prefer full addresses. Matching is normalized first (percent-encoding, backslashes, `.`/`..` segments, `_site/` mirror) then matched case-insensitively; a rule that names a directory covers everything beneath it, `*` stays inside a segment and `**` crosses segments. Overlapping rules only narrow: a reader must be granted by EVERY rule that matches the path. FAIL CLOSED — a block this engine cannot parse puts it in lockdown (nobody is an owner, everything is restricted), and a restricted path with no owner able to read it is denied to everyone rather than opened. Enforced at every choke point: static asset serving, per-user filtering of the served compiled artifacts (knowledge-pack items AND its #49 link graph; brain nodes, data.path and `references` edges), the chat agent's tool results, read_doc, and the served client.config.json (the access block itself is never shipped to a browser). `restricted_tools` withholds a whole tool from non-owners for output that is aggregate or entity-led and so cannot be path-redacted. LEGACY ALIASES: `admins` (= owners) and `owner_only` / `privateDocs` (= restricted) are accepted so an existing fork's config validates and runs unchanged; new engagements use `owners` + `restricted`.

owners.$comment: Full emails, or bare local-parts to match that local-part at any domain.

admins.$comment: Legacy alias for `owners`; merged with it.

restricted.$comment: Repo-relative path globs readable only by owners. A string entry is owners-only; an object entry additionally grants the readers it names.

owner_only.$comment: Legacy alias for `restricted`; merged with it.

privateDocs.$comment: Legacy alias for `restricted`; merged with it.

restricted_tools.$comment: Chat-agent tool names withheld from non-owners, e.g. "search_graph" when entity output cannot be path-redacted.

owner_only_tools.$comment: Legacy alias for `restricted_tools`; merged with it.

excludeFromBrain.$comment: Repo-relative globs kept OUT of the compiled brain (app/brain.json is a served artifact; an engagement that scopes some documents to a subset of readers points this at those paths so their titles/summaries are not published to everyone). Empty/absent = nothing excluded.

roadmap.description: Live GitHub Projects (v2) portfolio for /roadmap/ (scripts/gen-roadmap.py -> app/roadmap-live.json). Separate from issues.projects so the portfolio can span every product board. Best-effort; clean no-op when empty or gh is unavailable.

org.description: GitHub org that owns the Projects boards

metrics.description: Optional telemetry-pull seam for a metrics collector (scripts/gen-metrics.py style): per-source base URLs and tenant slugs the nightly pull reads. Auth never lives here (CI secrets only). Engagement-defined sources; kept permissive by design.

scope.description: Where this brain sits on the scope spine (federation > company > domain > project > workspace > person; agent for an autonomous node). A person scope owns its own canon and publishes upward only by consent. Ownership flows down, abstraction flows up, access narrows on the way up. Absent = a project-scope root named for client.slug.

parent.description: Scope address `<level>:<id>` of the parent brain, or null for a root.

profile.description: Ontology composition: `base` plus ORDERED `overlays`. Empty overlays fall back to brain-schema.json's legacy single-string profile.

federation.description: The publish-upward contract. CLOSED by default: nothing declared here means nothing leaves this scope. `publishes`/`withholds` are kind ids from brain-schema.json; `children` are the child brains this metarepo folds in via aggregate-brains.

enrollments.description: Signed consent to publish upward (#213), one entry per parent. Checked in full by scripts/federation_enrollment.py; `issued`/`signature` are written by `brain-publish-up.py sign`.

expires.description: Optional. No expiry unless set; past it the parent keeps what it holds and pauses intake until renewed.

deploy.description: Where the brain runs and which persistence is attached there. The target decides which projections are ALLOWED to exist, never what the brain is.

public.description: Astrolift: true only for a brain safe to serve without login; with no volume it renders a CDN static_site. Default false: a container behind the install's login gate.

image.description: Astrolift: the container image that serves a private brain (e.g. the context service), pinned by tag or digest.

portal.description: Presentation profile: which portal template (app/portal-templates.json) frames this brain. Independent of `profile` (the ontology).

view.description: Easy/advanced presentation only. Remembered kb_prefs.views choice for the authenticated viewer wins over the selected recipe scope default, then default (easy). Does not change permissions or writers.

recordViews.description: Presentation of an already authorized flat record collection; view scope is not access policy. Keys are explicit source-local identities and must be unique.

accessRule.$comment: One restricted-path entry (#53). A bare string is the path glob, owners-only. The object form takes `path` (or `glob`) plus optional `owners` who may read that entry in addition to the global owners.
